stem.text: Let \( f(x) = \frac{5 \left|{x + 5}\right|}{x + 6} \) for \( x \ne -6 \). Find all critical points of f.

answer_key.label: The only critical point of f is x = -5.

worked_solution.text: For x other than -5 and -6, \( f'(x) = \frac{5}{\left(x + 6\right)^{2}} \text{ for } x > -5 \text{ and } f'(x) = - \frac{5}{\left(x + 6\right)^{2}} \text{ for } x < -5 \). The derivative is never 0.
The numerator 5 is never 0, so \( f'(x) = 0 \) has no solution.
worked_solution.rule_named: critical point where the derivative is zero

worked_solution.text: At x = -5 the function is defined, \( f(-5) = 0 \), and the one-sided derivatives there have opposite signs, so the graph of f has a corner there; so the derivative fails to exist at an input in the domain and x = -5 is a critical point. At x = -6 the derivative also fails to exist, but f is not defined there, so x = -6 is not a critical point.
worked_solution.rule_named: critical point where the derivative fails to exist
